children: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Saturday urged banks to focus more on lending to small businesses, saying the broader economic benefits of such lending are significantly greater.

PTI reported that while speaking at a financial inclusion camp organised by Bank of Maharashtra at Waksai village in Mawal taluka, Pune district, Malhotra said a Rs 1,000-crore loan to a large business enterprise would benefit only one individual or business.

“However, if we provide the same amount to small enterprises, the overall impact and benefits could be at least a hundred times greater,” Malhotra said. He added that the impact could be a thousand times greater if the amount were distributed among micro-enterprise borrowers.

The career bureaucrat-turned-central banker said this was a “special appeal”, based on the gains he had witnessed among a wider section of people as banks increased their focus on rural areas and economically weaker segments.

“We must remember that development should be inclusive. When we talk about development, it must be development for everyone. It is important that we take all sections of society and all regions along with us,” he added.
Referring to the government's financial inclusion initiative, under which more than 60 crore bank accounts have been opened, Malhotra said the focus must now extend to financial and digital literacy.
Banking services are increasingly being accessed through digital platforms, he said, underlining the importance of exercising caution while using digital banking services.
He also cautioned people against fraudulent financial schemes targeting unsuspecting investors.

“If someone approaches you with an offer promising returns of 20%, 30% or even 40% over a short period, you should be extremely cautious. Such unusually high returns are often associated with hidden risks or fraudulent schemes,” he said.
Malhotra urged people never to share their one-time passwords (OTPs) and to be careful about clicking on unknown links or responding to suspicious messages.

“I would strongly encourage all of you to adopt digital banking services, but do so responsibly and with complete awareness. We must ensure that people are protected from all kinds of digital fraud,” he said.

The camp, which saw a turnout of more than 500 people, aims to bring essential banking services and government-backed social security schemes closer to the community. Malhotra said such camps would be held across the country until December 31.

Bank of Maharashtra Managing Director and Chief Executive Nidhu Saxena and other banking sector officials also attended the camp, which is part of the Department of Financial Services' (DFS) nationwide Financial Inclusion Saturation Campaign.

Saxena said the bank had expanded its business correspondent network to 10,000 from 3,000 two years ago. It has conducted 3,691 camps so far, including those organised by the regional rural bank it sponsors.

title: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra urges banks to step up lending to small, micro enterprises for greater economic gains
